title: MIT researchers use AI to stabilize RNA vaccines for room temperature storage
excerpt: The algorithm optimized lipid nanoparticle formulations to allow vaccines to remain stable at room temperature for up to one year.
bodyHtml:
Researchers at MIT published a study in Nature Biotechnology on September 28, 2026, detailing a new method to increase the heat resistance of mRNA vaccines.

By utilizing an AI algorithm, the team optimized the lipid nanoparticles, which are fatty particles used to deliver mRNA, allowing the vaccines to remain stable at room temperature for up to a year or at nearly 100 degrees Fahrenheit for two months.

The algorithm enabled the team to identify effective formulations using small datasets, significantly reducing the number of experiments required.

The researchers tested the stabilized particles in mice, which produced immune responses equivalent to those generated by standard RNA Covid-19 vaccines. The study also demonstrated that the AI could be applied to stabilize different lipid nanoparticle formulations, including those similar to the Pfizer Covid-19 vaccine.
topic: New formulation helps RNA vaccines withstand high temperatures
